findings.description: Original criticism retained verbatim: Recoverable HTTP parser failures still abort the entire public metadata refresh. BadStatusLine and LineTooLong inherit HTTPException, not OSError or IncompleteRead, and escape default_fetch and the CLI. This leaves the DG1-02 per-row error boundary incomplete; a malformed status line can also be echoed verbatim in the traceback. MODIFIED (widened): the escaping set was larger than the two named classes. A bare HTTPException (header-count limit), UnknownProtocol (echoes remote version text), LineTooLong while reading a chunk size, InvalidURL from a remote redirect Location port, and RecursionError from JSON nested deeper than the interpreter limit also aborted the refresh.
findings.evidence: Original gate evidence retained: real urllib opener -> HTTPSConnection -> HTTPResponse, in-memory socket, fault on request 12/26; JSON and Markdown CLI each exit 1 with traceback after 12 fetches; BadStatusLine echoes /remote-body-marker; 4 failed in 5.29s. Independently reproduced here on frozen e6f0963e (gate reproducer: 4 failed, 12/26, marker echoed) and by the new owner RED (18 failed with the predicted classes). Original source: bakeoff_intake.py:309 caught only (OSError, http.client.IncompleteRead); :313-314 caught only ValueError around json.loads. Fix: :309-313 catch the documented http.client.HTTPException family with OSError -> FetchResult(error='network_error') -> existing unverified/network_error via audit_one. The exception message is discarded, so no remote status, header or Location text reaches a renderer or stderr. :318-321 catch (ValueError, RecursionError) at json.loads only -> existing error/malformed_json with http_status 200. HTTPError (URLError subclass, caught earlier) keeps 401/403/404/429/5xx/418 distinctions; verified through real urllib. InvalidURL is deliberately inside the family: the probe proved a remote 302 Location reaches it, and loaded rows come from the validated sealed registry and intake. TypeError/AttributeError/KeyError/RuntimeError still propagate (guards; broad-except mutant caught). Tests: test_actual_urllib_protocol_failure_is_one_typed_row_and_refresh_continues (14 cases, all 26 typed records, failed repo identity, 25 unchanged peers, latest/pipeline/license null, no marker, empty stdout/stderr); test_cli_protocol_failure_has_no_traceback_and_does_not_echo_remote_text (4 subprocess cases); test_actual_urllib_keeps_http_status_distinctions (7); test_actual_urllib_valid_unicode_row_is_classified_normally; test_default_fetch_does_not_swallow_programming_errors (4). Canon: CAL-02 https://github.com/darce/heuristics-canon/blob/v0.26.2/lexicons/ml-systems.md#cal-02 ; CARD-03 https://github.com/darce/heuristics-canon/blob/v0.26.2/reasoning/designed-unknown.md ; CARD-08 and TEST-06 https://github.com/darce/heuristics-canon/blob/v0.26.2/reasoning/falsification-disconfirmers.md , https://github.com/darce/heuristics-canon/blob/v0.26.2/lexicons/engineering.md#test-06 ; TEST-15 via CARD-11 https://github.com/darce/heuristics-canon/blob/v0.26.2/reasoning/measurement-integrity.md

findings.description: Same boundary, different class: a remote 3xx whose Location holds an unbalanced IPv6 literal (e.g. https://[x/...) makes urllib's HTTPRedirectHandler raise a bare ValueError('Invalid IPv6 URL') out of urlopen, which still aborts the 26-row refresh.
findings.evidence: Pre-RED probe on frozen source and the committed strict xfail test_malformed_redirect_location_is_an_open_residual (raises=ValueError) both reproduce it; the broad-except mutant turned it XPASS(strict), proving the test is live. Not fixed by design: the only catch that covers it at default_fetch is ValueError around urlopen. That would also swallow local configuration errors such as a malformed proxy environment, and violates the brief's no-broad-catch constraint. Exit with a designed unknown here needs a coordinator decision (CAL-02/CARD-03), not a silent widening.
findings.fix: Proposed, not applied: either (a) install an opener whose redirect handler maps a ValueError from Location parsing to an HTTPError/typed row, or (b) accept a ValueError catch scoped to the urlopen call with the local-config tradeoff recorded. Then flip the strict xfail to a normal assertion.

Protocol failures report http_status=null even when a status line was parsed before a body-phase failure (e.g. chunk-size LineTooLong). This keeps the existing A2 IncompleteRead convention; recording 200 there is possible but would change existing behavior.

Not examined: urllib follows redirects to other hosts (HTTPRedirectHandler) and reports the redirected repo's sha as the pinned repo's latest. That is an audit-identity question outside DG2-01, with no change made.

Only the owner test module ran (--noconftest, plugin autoload disabled, required_plugins cleared). Three known unknown-config warnings are retained. No full suite, sealed-loader suite or B2/B3 suites. An outer timeout of 300s bounded each run.
Tests use urllib.request._opener (private stdlib global) to keep the real urlopen function in the path with ProxyHandler({}); this relies on CPython 3.12 urlopen internals.
